They are cold under the earth. Shall we give fire to the dead? We shall give fire at the feast, and I shall pour mead for them.

english: Hero, an eagle is flying above the army! I have seen it. It flies on the right. What sign does the eagle give? Perkʷunos is giving us victory. We shall overpower the enemies. english: Mother-in-law, the fire on the hearth became cold in the night. Who was protecting the fire? I was protecting it; sleep seized me. That is a bad sign. Fire has gone away from this house. What shall I do? Take fire from the villagers, and praise Fire with a song. I shall praise him in the evenings. He will return home.

english: Brother, a crane flew up on the right; let us hunt! I caught sight of it on my left hand. You are standing opposite me! Then the crane was speaking to you. Go hunting; I shall stay with the cattle. If I kill a pig, will you eat it? I shall eat it, and I shall praise the crane.

english: Sister, I have seen a great dream. Say it! Was a god speaking to you? A god was not speaking; I was eating a whole ox at a feast. When you woke up, what did you do? I was hungry, and I ate up the grain of my brother. Then your dream was true: you ate up a feast. Our brother will not laugh.

english: Uncle, our dog was crying the whole night. Toward which home is it turned? Toward the home of the old shepherd. Death is coming to the old shepherd. Shall I tell his sons? Do not tell them; go to him and sit with him. I shall go to him at dawn.

english: Uncle, a wolf crossed our path at dawn. Did it come from the left hand? It came from the left hand, and it looked at me. Did you become afraid of the wolf? I did not become afraid; I called the dogs. The wolves are coming to the sheep. Protect the sheep in the night with the dogs. I shall protect them, and I shall not sleep. Will you sit with me in the night? I shall sit with you, and I shall sing.

english: Sister, I have seen our mother in sleep. She died in the winter. What was she saying to you? She asked for her own cup. She is thirsty. The cup lies in the house. We forgot it. Let us give it to our mother. In the evening let us fill the cup with mead and lay it in the earth. Then she will rest.

english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

english: Husband, Dawn came to me in sleep. Dawn, the daughter of Sky? She was beautiful, and she gave me a flower. Where is the flower now? I woke up, and the flower vanished. Do not weep. May Dawn give you a child! May the gods hear you!

english: Husband, wake up! My teeth fell in a dream. When did you catch sight of it? It was dawning. Dreams of dawn are true. Who will die? Your grandmother is old. Go to her quickly. I shall go on this day, and I shall give her honey. Tell her your dream.

It leaves, and at dawn it comes back. If it does not come back, what will happen? Then the sleeping mortal dies. Do not tremble: it returned unharmed. At night I shall fly again!

english: Dear friend, in sleep I caught sight of a white horse. Where did the horse run? It ran toward the dawn, and it did not come back. A white horse is fame. Your fame will be imperishable. May the gods hear your words! They hear them; Dyēus hears all things. Let us drink mead, friend!

english: Grandfather, enemies drove off our cattle in the night. Did I not tell you? The crane cried three times in the evening. I heard the crane, and I did not heed it. Whoever does not heed the gods, that man's cattle vanish. What shall I do now? Call your brothers and follow them. If they are many, shall we not die? Perkʷunos will strike them down. Do not fear!

english: Master, your cow bore two calves in the night. Are they twins? They are twins, and they are white. The gods are giving us wealth. This year will be good. What shall we do for the calves? Cherish them, and pour milk of their mother to Fire. I shall pour it at dawn.
